files.Summary: Converts an into an Apache Arrow .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Arrow.ArrowReadOptions
files.Summary: Options for converting a sheet with .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Arrow.ArrowWriteOptions
files.Summary: Options for writing a record batch with .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.ExcelSheetVisibility
files.Summary: Whether a sheet is shown in the workbook's tab bar. The values match the on-disk encoding every format uses for it (XLSX's state attribute, XLSB's BrtBundleSh.hsState, XLS's BoundSheet8.hsState).

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Parser.CsvEnumerable<T>
files.Summary: Lazily projects CSV rows into T instances by binding each property to a fixed field index, for both synchronous and asynchronous enumeration.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Parser.ExcelCellReader<TValue>
files.Summary: Reads a non-empty cell into a value of type TValue. Every built-in reader exposed by matches this shape, so a source-generated or hand-written map can plug either a built-in reader or a custom one into .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Parser.ExcelCellReaders
files.Summary: The built-in cell readers ExcelParser<T>'s reflection path already uses, exposed as instances for a source-generated or hand-written map to plug into without duplicating the conversion logic.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Parser.ExcelColumnAttribute
files.Summary: Maps a property to a worksheet column by header name. Apply more than once to accept alternate header spellings for the same property.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Parser.ExcelConverterAttribute
files.Summary: Binds a custom to a property. The converter type must implement for the property's exact type and expose a public parameterless constructor.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Parser.ExcelEnumerable<T>
files.Summary: Lazily projects XLSX rows into T instances, for both synchronous and asynchronous enumeration.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Parser.ExcelIgnoreAttribute
files.Summary: Excludes a property from both parsing and record writing: no column is read into it and none is written from it. Use for computed or transient properties.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Parser.ExcelParseException
files.Summary: Thrown when a bound column's cell is non-empty but fails to parse into the target property type and the parser is configured to throw on parse failures (rather than silently keep the property at its default). See .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Parser.ExcelParser<T>
files.Summary: Parses rows from an Excel or CSV sheet into instances of T. Create one with : reflects over [ExcelColumn]/[ExcelRequired]/[ExcelConverter] attributes, uses the [ExcelSerializable] source-generated map, and takes a map configured at runtime.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Parser.ExcelParser
files.Summary: Creates instances.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Parser.ExcelParserOptions
files.Summary: Options controlling how locates the header row, matches header text to bound properties, and handles cells that fail to parse.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Parser.ExcelPropertySetter<TModel, TValue>
files.Summary: Assigns value to a property of model. The source generator emits this as a direct property assignment (e.g. static (ref T m, V v) => m.Prop = v) — no delegate compilation at runtime.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Parser.ExcelRequiredAttribute
files.Summary: Marks a property whose column must be present in the header row; parsing throws when the header is read if no matching name is found. By default every data row's cell must also be non-empty (and must parse successfully — a non-empty but unparsable cell fails the same way as a blank one), throwing on the first row that fails either check. Set to true to require only the column's presence. Contrast with , which governs parse-failure behavior only for non-required columns.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Parser.ExcelRowContext
files.Summary: Settings a cell reader, converter or row parser needs to convert a cell, handed to every , and call.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Parser.ExcelRowMapBuilder<T>
files.Summary: Accumulates a row-to-property binding for T, fed either by the source generator (feature A) or by a hand-written implementation. Mirrors, without reflection, exactly what TypeMapper<T>.Build() produces from attributes.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Parser.ExcelRowParser<TModel>
files.Summary: Reads a matched, non-empty cell and assigns the result directly onto model in one call, instead of going through a separate + pair. Plug this into when a single fused delegate (e.g. one emitted by the [ExcelSerializable] source generator) should replace what would otherwise be two indirect calls per bound cell per row.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Parser.ExcelSerializableAttribute
files.Summary: Marks a type for the source generator to produce and implementations for, from its [ExcelColumn]/[ExcelRequired]/[ExcelIgnore] attributes — the same source TypeMapper<T>'s reflection path reads, but resolved at compile time. The marked type (and every type it is nested inside, if any) must be declared partial, since the generator emits into an additional part of the same declaration.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Parser.HeaderNormalization
files.Summary: Flags controlling how header text is normalized before being matched against or a property name.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Parser.IExcelCellConverter<T>
files.Summary: Converts a matched cell into a property value. Implement this and attach the implementation with [ExcelConverter(typeof(MyConverter))] for types the built-in parsers do not handle (money strings, custom date formats, domain value objects, ...).

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Parser.IExcelRowMap<T>
files.Summary: Implemented by the source generator (feature A) — or by hand, before the generator runs — on the row model type itself, which must be partial. The static abstract member turns "no map was generated for this model" into a compile error (T fails the where T : IExcelRowMap<T> constraint on ) instead of a silent runtime fallback to reflection.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Cell
files.Summary: A single worksheet cell's value, exposed as a zero-allocation view over the reader's underlying buffers. Only valid for the lifetime of the row it was read from — do not store it past that point.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.CellType
files.Summary: Identifies the kind of value a holds.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Csv.CsvDialect
files.Summary: The delimiter, quote, and encoding inferred by from a sample of a delimited-text source.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Csv.CsvReader.Enumerator
files.Summary: A forward-only cursor over a source's records, reading either synchronously or asynchronously.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Csv.CsvReader
files.Summary: An open delimited-text (CSV-style) source, exposed as a workbook with a single, unnamed sheet.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Csv.CsvReaderOptions
files.Summary: The delimited-text settings for a CSV source, carried by .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Csv.CsvSheet
files.Summary: The single, unnamed sheet of a . A value that holds no resources.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Csv.CsvSniffer
files.Summary: Infers a CSV dialect (delimiter, quote, encoding) from a sample of a delimited-text source.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Csv.CsvSnifferOptions
files.Summary: Options controlling how infers a .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Excel
files.Summary: Entry point for opening Excel and CSV workbooks. / and their async counterparts auto-detect XLSX/XLSB/XLS from the file's signature and return a format-agnostic ; the From*/FromXls*/FromXlsb*/FromCsv* methods open a specific, known format directly.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.ExcelEncryptionException
files.Summary: Thrown when an encrypted workbook cannot be opened. Inspect to decide what to do: only and are worth prompting a user about — the other two are terminal, and retrying with another password will never help.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.ExcelEncryptionReason
files.Summary: Why an encrypted workbook could not be opened.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.ExcelFileFormat
files.Summary: Identifies the on-disk Excel file format a workbook was read from or is to be written as.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.ExcelLimitExceededException
files.Summary: Thrown when reading a workbook would exceed one of the resource limits configured on (e.g. decompressed size, a single cell's byte length, shared-string table size, or ZIP entry count), guarding against maliciously or accidentally oversized files.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.ExcelPassword
files.Summary: A workbook password. Deliberately a class rather than a record: a record's synthesized ToString would print the password, and this type is held by , which is a record — so one logger.LogDebug("{Options}", options) would leak it. below is what makes that safe.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.ExcelReaderOptions
files.Summary: Resource limits and behavior toggles applied when opening and reading a workbook or a CSV source. Exceeding a byte or entry-count limit throws .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.ExcelSheetList<TSheet>
files.Summary: The sheets of a workbook, in workbook order. Indexing or enumerating the list opens nothing.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.ExcelTable
files.Summary: An Excel table (a range formatted with "Format as Table", stored as a ListObject): its name, its position on its sheet and its columns.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.IExcelRowEnumerator
files.Summary: A forward-only cursor over a sheet's rows, implemented by every concrete format's row enumerator and driven either synchronously () or asynchronously ().

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.IExcelSheet<TEnumerator>
files.Summary: One sheet's rows, typed to the concrete enumerator it hands out (TEnumerator) so callers read without boxing to .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.IExcelSheet
files.Summary: A sheet of an : its position, name and visibility, and its rows.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.IExcelWorkbook
files.Summary: An open workbook of any supported format (XLSX, XLSB, XLS, CSV): its sheets and the state they share. Sheets are obtained from it and read independently.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.IRowAccumulator<TSelf, TModel>
files.Summary: Folds typed rows read by SheetParallel.AggregateAsync into a result. Each partition of the sheet gets its own instance.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.IRowRecord<TSelf>
files.Summary: A typed row that parses itself from a , for .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Row
files.Summary: A single worksheet row, exposed as a zero-allocation view over the reader's underlying buffers. Only valid for the lifetime of the enumeration that produced it — do not store it past that point.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.RowAction<TState>
files.Summary: Processes one row into the state owned by the partition that read it.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.RowAggregation<TState>
files.Summary: A fold over rows expressed as three functions, for . Carries the same contract as , without requiring a type.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.RowCell
files.Summary: A cell paired with its column index, as produced by .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.RowCellEnumerator
files.Summary: Enumerates the populated cells of a , in ascending column order, skipping gaps. Supports foreach via the duck-typed enumerator pattern (ref structs cannot implement ).

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Schema.ExcelColumnSchema
files.Summary: One column's guessed shape, as returned by .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Schema.ExcelColumnType
files.Summary: A column's inferred or declared value type, as produced by .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Schema.SchemaInferenceOptions
files.Summary: Options for guessing a column schema with .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.SheetDataReader
files.Summary: Adapts one to , so it can feed SqlBulkCopy, DataTable.Load, Dapper, or any other ADO.NET consumer directly.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.SheetDataReaderOptions
files.Summary: Options for adapting a sheet to with .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.SheetParallel
files.Summary: Reads a sheet of any format across several threads: ParseAsync yields typed rows in source order, ForEachAsync hands each row to a callback on the worker threads, and AggregateAsync folds rows into one accumulator per partition.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.SheetParallelOptions
files.Summary: Options for reading a sheet across several threads with .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Xls.XlsSheet
files.Summary: One sheet of an . A value that holds no resources; each enumerator it creates reads independently.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Xls.XlsWorkbook.Enumerator
files.Summary: Enumerates the rows of a single worksheet in an , supporting both synchronous and asynchronous iteration.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Xls.XlsWorkbook
files.Summary: An open legacy BIFF8 (.xls) workbook. Its sheets are read independently, each through synchronous and asynchronous enumeration.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Xlsb.XlsbSheet
files.Summary: One sheet of an . A value that holds no resources; each enumerator it creates reads independently.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Xlsb.XlsbWorkbook.Enumerator
files.Summary: Forward-only enumerator over an sheet's rows.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Xlsb.XlsbWorkbook
files.Summary: An open binary Excel (.xlsb / BIFF12) workbook. Its sheets are read independently, each streaming its cells without loading the whole file into memory.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Xlsx.XlsxSheet
files.Summary: One sheet of an . A value that holds no resources; each enumerator it creates reads independently.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Xlsx.XlsxWorkbook.Enumerator
files.Summary: Forward-only enumerator over an sheet's rows.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Reader.Xlsx.XlsxWorkbook
files.Summary: An open Office Open XML (.xlsx) workbook. Its sheets are read independently, each streaming its cells without loading the whole file into memory.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.CellStyle
files.Summary: A column- or row-level cell style: number format, bold, and italic. Register one with .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.Csv.CsvNewLine
files.Summary: The byte sequence a writes after each record.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.Csv.CsvRowWriter
files.Summary: Writes the fields of a single CSV row, quoting a field only when it contains the delimiter, quote character, carriage return, or line feed.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.Csv.CsvSheetWriter
files.Summary: The single sheet of a CSV "workbook". Adapts the flat to the contract that record writing drives.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.Csv.CsvWorkbookWriter
files.Summary: Writes a CSV file through the contract. A CSV file holds exactly one sheet, so only a single call is supported.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.Csv.CsvWriterOptions
files.Summary: Configures the dialect, encoding, and record terminator used when writing a CSV file.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.ExcelRecordLayout<T>
files.Summary: How ' WriteRecordsAsync turns a T into a header row and one row per record. Create one with : reflects over the record type, and uses the [ExcelSerializable] source-generated map.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.ExcelRecordLayout
files.Summary: Creates instances.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.ExcelRecordMapBuilder<T, TRow>
files.Summary: Accumulates a property-to-column write plan for T, fed either by the source generator (feature A) or by a hand-written implementation. The write-side counterpart to .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.ExcelTableOptions
files.Summary: Configures an Excel table written with .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.IExcelCellWriter<T>
files.Summary: Writes a value of type T as a cell of a row, for use with the [ExcelConverter] attribute on a property that writes. Implement this alongside IExcelCellConverter<T> on the same converter type to round-trip a custom type through both writing (via ) and reading (via ExcelParser<T>). A single instance is shared across every row and thread, so implementations must be stateless and thread-safe.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.IExcelRecordMap<T>
files.Summary: Implemented by the source generator (feature A) — or by hand, before the generator runs — on the record type itself, which must be partial. Generated in the same partial as , since both maps derive from the same property list and attributes.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.IRowWriter
files.Summary: Writes one row's cells in column order, starting at the first column. Obtained from ; each Write/ call advances to the next column, so cells must be written left-to-right with no way to revisit an earlier column. Disposing the row writer (sync or async) finalizes the row and returns it to the sheet. Calling any member after disposal throws .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.ISheetWriter<TRow>
files.Summary: Writes one sheet's rows to the workbook. Obtained from ; a caller optionally sets column styles and widths, writes rows in order via , then ends the sheet. The sheet's leading structure is written when the first row starts, or at for a sheet with no rows.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.ITableSheetWriter<TRow>
files.Summary: A sheet writer that can write Excel tables (ranges formatted with "Format as Table"). Implemented by the XLSX and XLSB sheet writers.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.IWorkbookWriter<TSheet>
files.Summary: Writes a whole workbook (XLSX, XLSB, XLS or CSV) to a destination stream, one sheet at a time. Implementations open the underlying stream/archive on construction, so a caller only needs to add sheets with and dispose the workbook (or call then dispose) when finished.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.ParallelSheetWriterExtensions
files.Summary: Record writes that format and compress batches of rows on several threads and write them in order. Memory is bounded by batches of rows.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.ParallelWriteOptions
files.Summary: Configures the parallel record writes of .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.SheetWriterExtensions
files.Summary: Convenience methods layered on : write a whole collection of records to a sheet in one call, driving the start-row/write/dispose lifecycle per record.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.Xls.XlsRowWriter
files.Summary: Writes the cells of a single row of a BIFF8 (.xls) sheet.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.Xls.XlsSheetWriter
files.Summary: Writes a single sheet of a BIFF8 (.xls) workbook, buffering cell records in memory until the workbook is finalized. Rows beyond the BIFF8 65,536-row cap spill into an auto-generated continuation sheet.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.Xls.XlsWorkbookWriter
files.Summary: Writes a workbook to the legacy BIFF8 (.xls) binary format.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.Xls.XlsWriterOptions
files.Summary: Configures how a BIFF8 (.xls) workbook is written.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.Xlsb.XlsbCell
files.Summary: An immutable, typed cell value for , created via one of the factory overloads.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.Xlsb.XlsbRowWriter
files.Summary: Writes the cells of a single row into an .xlsb worksheet, one column at a time.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.Xlsb.XlsbSheetWriter
files.Summary: Writes a single worksheet's rows into an .xlsb workbook produced by .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.Xlsb.XlsbWorkbookWriter
files.Summary: Writes an .xlsb workbook (BIFF12 binary format) to a stream, one sheet at a time.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.Xlsb.XlsbWriterOptions
files.Summary: Configures how an XLSB package is written.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.Xlsx.XlsxRowWriter
files.Summary: Writes the cells of a single worksheet row into an XLSX row buffer; reused across rows by .

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.Xlsx.XlsxSheetWriter
files.Summary: Writes a single worksheet's XML into an XLSX ZIP archive, buffering rows and flushing them to the entry stream once they cross a size threshold.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.Xlsx.XlsxWorkbookWriter
files.Summary: Writes a workbook to the XLSX (Office Open XML) format, streaming each sheet's rows into a ZIP archive as they're written.

files.Title: ExcelReader.Core.Writer.Xlsx.XlsxWriterOptions
files.Summary: Configures how an XLSX package is written.
